failing.note: OpenSSL QUICv1/TLS1.3 handshake succeeds from the same host, so this is a netz client interop issue rather than reachability. The netz client receives no server response across five retries.

packet_number_fix.change: InitialResponseFilter records the accepted packet number; openInitialCryptoFlightFrom starts at that number and is bounded by the initial-flight deadline.
packet_number_fix.remaining_failure: The handshake still times out after the ServerHello. Forcing X25519-only also times out, so the key exchange group is not the cause; the next target is the server Handshake flight or coalesced Initial/Handshake packet processing.
packet_number_fix.result: The client now processes the server Initial packet 1 and parses the ServerHello (AES-128-GCM-SHA256, X25519MLKEM768).

root_cause_analysis: The quic.tech server responds with an ACK-only Initial packet number zero followed by an Initial packet number one carrying CRYPTO offset zero.
The filter originally rejected the ACK-only packet; openInitialCryptoFlightFrom then expected packet number zero and discarded packet one.
The filter now records the accepted packet number, so packet one is processed and the ServerHello is parsed.
The handshake still times out after the ServerHello; the remaining boundary is the server Handshake flight or the X25519MLKEM768 shared-secret path.
Accepting the ACK-only packet unconditionally was tested and reintroduced the documented split-ClientHello deadlock, so the filter still rejects ACK-only later fragments.
x25519_only_test: The fetch example was temporarily restricted to key_exchange_groups=&.{.x25519}; quic.tech still returned HandshakeTimeout after the ServerHello.
